sentences.text:
The facts leading to presentation of the petition, referred to above, are these:
(i).

The appellant had lodged a complaint against her husband (Nirmal) and three of her in-laws (respondents 2 to 4), 1 impugned order 2 S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous (Petition) No.378 of 2022 17:52:17 IST Reason:
3 Cr. PC which gave rise to a First Information Report 4 under Sections 498A, 406,
323, 341, 354A, 354D, 376 and 511 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

(ii). In course of investigation, the appellants statement under Section 164, Cr. PC was recorded by the Investigating Officer wherein she levelled allegations against all the accused of having committed the aforesaid offences.
(iii).
The Investigating Officer, upon completion of investigation, submitted a police report (charge-sheet) under Section 173(2), Cr. PC arraigning Nirmal only as an accused.

sentences.text: (iv). On 31.10.2019, cognizance was taken by the relevant Magistrate against Nirmal.

Obviously,
cognizance was not taken against the respondents 2 to 4, since they did not figure as accused in the police report.

(v). Alleging that copy of the police report had not been furnished to her, the appellant had moved the Magistrate with an application seeking an order for taking cognizance of offence under Section 190, Cr. PC against the respondents 2 to 4.
Such application came to be dismissed by the Magistrate by an order dated 15.02.2020.

It was reasoned by the Magistrate that since 4 FIR Crl.A. @ SLP(Crl.)
No.1984/2025 cognizance was taken against Nirmal on 31.10.2019 and cognizance not having been taken against the respondents 2 to 4 based on the police report that was filed, allowing the application of the appellant would amount to a review of the order dated 31.10.2019 which was not permissible in terms of Section 362, Cr. PC.

(vi). It is not in dispute that Nirmal has since passed away on 18.06.2020 and, therefore,
proceedings against him have abated.
(viii).

It is also not in dispute that the order dated 15.02.2020 of the Magistrate having been upheld by the revisional court, the appellant moved a petition5 under Section 482, Cr. PC which is pending before the High Court.

(ix). Months after Nirmal passed away and after having approached the High Court questioning the order dated 15.02.2020, the appellant was advised to move the High Court a second time challenging the order dated 31.10.2019 not taking cognizance of the offences alleged against the respondents 2 to 4, whereupon the impugned order was passed giving rise to the present appeal.
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant, the State as well as the respondents 2 to 4 and perused the materials on record.

5 S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 8362 of 2021 Crl.A. @ SLP(Crl.) No.1984/2025 5. Section 173(2)(ii) of the Cr. PC 6 casts an obligation on the Investigating Officer to communicate the action taken by him to the person by whom information relating to commission of the offence was first given.

sentences.text: 6. It does not appear from the impugned order that the High Court addressed the grievance of the appellant that she was not served the police report and, thus, the action taken by the Investigating Officer upon investigation of the FIR was not communicated to her.

Incidentally, the appellant had categorically alleged that because of lack of communication, she was not aware of the contents of the police report and hence, could not exercise her right under Section 173(8), Cr. PC to lodge a protest petition.

sentences.text: Perusal of the impugned order of the High Court further reveals that it noted the death of Nirmal which had resulted in abatement of the proceedings against him.
However, the High Court seems to have missed to address the real point in controversy while dismissing the petition filed by the appellant.

The cryptic order passed by the High Court has rightly been criticized by the appellant by urging that the respondents 2 to 4 have been allowed to go unscathed despite there being allegations in the statement recorded by her under Section 164 6 The officer shall communicate, in such manner as may be prescribed by the State Government, the action taken by him, to the person, if any, by whom the information relating to the commission of the offence was first given.
Crl . A.

@
SLP(Crl.) No.1984/2025 of the Cr. PC revealing their complicity and without the real point that was urged being noticed and addressed

. In our opinion, the High Court ought to have examined whether in due compliance with Section 173(2)(ii), Cr. PC, the appellant had been communicated the action taken by the Investigating Officer on the FIR.
Depending on the status of communication or the lack of it, the logical consequences should have followed.

8. Since the High Court did not address the concern expressed by the appellant but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the claim raised by her, we are of the considered view that interest of justice would be sufficiently served if Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No.378 of 2022 is revived for fresh consideration by the High Court and for decision based on the contentions to be urged by the parties.
9. For the reasons stated aforesaid, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned order dated 10.10.2024 stands set aside and Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No.378 of 2022 is restored to its original file and number.
The same may be heard with Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 8362 of 2021 to avoid conflict of decisions.

10. The High court is requested to decide the said petitions, subject to its convenience, preferably within four months from date.
11.
All contentions of the parties are left open.
Pending applications, if any, shall stand closed.
